epitaph: The LCW Heavyweight Title changed hands across 29 recorded reigns, from a 14 February 1997 inaugural tournament — won by Tower — through Johnny Hardcore's own 14 May 2000 tournament win over a vacant title, its own final entry in the surviving record; HICAL alone held it four separate times.
name: LCW Heavyweight Title
notes: Full reign-by-reign chain (29 title changes across 30 recorded holders, 14 Feb 1997 – 14 May 2000) structured from the fed's own served ledger (promotions/lcw-1997/archive/heavyweight-title.html).

epitaph: The LCW World Hardcore Title (billed the World Extreme Title in the fed's own rulebook) survives from a pre-history holder, "The Stalker" Steve Caslu, whose own reign predates the ledger's own 4 August 1998 opening entry, through 17 more recorded reigns to "The King of Slack" Chris Egerton's own 16 April 2000 win over Cuchulain, its own final entry in the surviving record.
name: LCW World Hardcore Title
notes: Full reign-by-reign chain (17 title changes, plus the ledger's own pre-history holder, 4 Aug 1998 – 16 Apr 2000) structured from the fed's own served ledger (promotions/lcw-1997/archive/hardcore-title.html).

epitaph: The LCW Television Title changed hands seven times across the fed's own surviving ledger, from a 24 October 1999 debut tournament through Johnny Wannabe's own second reign, won from "IRA" Sean Fein on 14 May 2000, its own final entry in the surviving record.
name: LCW Television Title
notes: Full reign-by-reign chain (7 entries, 24 Oct 1999 – 14 May 2000) structured from the fed's own served ledger (promotions/lcw-1997/archive/television-title.html).

epitaph: The LCW Tag Team Title changed hands across 35 recorded reigns, from an inaugural tournament won by the Travellers on 14 February 1997 through Blood Brothers' own 16 April 2000 win over the Wannabes, its own final entry in the surviving record — including one team tracked continuously across four billed names (the Insiders, then Pain, then the Sylvania Brothers, then the Outlaw Enforcers) and two vacancies.
name: LCW Tag Team Title
notes: Full reign-by-reign chain (30 entries, including two vacancies and one team's own four-name rename chain tracked continuously by the ledger's own numbering, Feb 1997 – Apr 2000) structured from the fed's own served ledger (promotions/lcw-1997/archive/tag-team-title.html).

name: LCW World Cruiserweight Title
notes: Named in the fed's own rulebook (promotions/lcw-1997/archive/rulebook.html) but carries no dedicated ledger; the one reign structured here is drawn from two dated snapshots (the Champions and Rankings page, 6 Jan 2000 capture; the Upcoming Events page's own billed title match, 7 Mar 2000 capture) rather than a won/lost chain.
epitaph: The LCW World Cruiserweight Title survives only as a snapshot: Angel of Death held it by 6 January 2000 and was still billed defending it seven weeks later, against Trevor Kidd on a card whose own result was never captured — no ledger names an earlier champion or records how Angel of Death himself won it.
